title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Reveals Tiny AI Robots at GTC Berlin 2026

lines.text: These tiny robots can walk, fall and get back up, and nobody programmed those moves step by step.
At NVIDIA's keynote in Berlin, Jensen Huang brought out four little two-legged robots, about twenty-five centimetres tall.
lines.label: 25 CM

lines.text: They walked, they tumbled, and when he told them to sit, stand or lie down, they did it.
Each one has a camera, a laser that measures distance, motion sensors that feel every tilt, and fifteen small motors.
lines.label: 15 MOTORS

lines.text: But the clever part is how they learned to move.
Engineers let them practise thousands of times inside a simulation, and every step closer to the goal earned a reward.
lines.label: PRACTICE

lines.text: That practice becomes one skill the robot carries over to the real world, for walking, kicking, grabbing, even getting up after a fall.
Now, this was a stage demo.
Change the floor or the task, and it can still lose its balance.
What it really shows is that robot experiments just got a lot cheaper, not that robots got a human brain.
lines.label: CHEAPER

lines.text: Follow the channel for the engineering behind every robot demo.
So, would you trust one of these in your home, or is it just a lab toy?
